## Blocking Findings

### [correctness, requirements] Production weighting never sees affected-criterion declarations — `src/lib/overdeck/substrate-bug-weights-service.ts:58`
The production default source for `listSubstrateBugWeights()` is `listInWindow`, cast to `SubstrateBugInput[]`, but the real `FlywheelSubstrateBug` projection does not include issue `body` or `labels`. The service then calls `parseAffectedCriteria(bug.body, bug.labels)`, so real rows reach the parser with both inputs missing and collapse to `affectedCriteria: []`, `weight: 0`, and `"no affected criteria declared"`.

This blocks FR-4 because the route and CLI return weighted rows, but the live production path cannot observe the `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion` trailer or `affects-criterion-N` labels required to compute metric-aware weights. Fix by making the production data source supply supported body/label or parsed-criteria data before parsing, and remove the unsafe cast so TypeScript enforces the required shape.

### [correctness] Criterion 6 weights read a nonexistent top-level ratio — `src/lib/overdeck/substrate-bug-weight.ts:24`
`CRITERION_META` maps criterion 6 to `valueField: 'ratio'`, but criterion 6 telemetry is compound: `value` contains `simple`, `medium`, and `complex` bucket objects with ratios, while `target` contains `maxRatio`. `numericSubfield()` only reads a top-level field, so criterion 6 gets the status floor but never the normalized distance from the worst bucket ratio to the target.

This makes red time-consistency bugs with very different ratios rank the same. Fix by normalizing criterion 6 explicitly, using the highest finite bucket ratio and comparing it to `target.maxRatio`, with a focused regression test.

### [performance] New weights route returns an unbounded result set — `src/dashboard/server/routes/flywheel-substrate-bug-weights.ts:16`
`GET /api/flywheel/substrate-bug-weights` accepts a caller-provided `window`, loads all matching substrate bugs, maps and sorts the full result, and serializes every row without a maximum window, limit, cursor, or pagination.

The route is a new HTTP request path, so its memory, sorting cost, and response size are unbounded by request. Fix by adding a bounded response contract, such as clamping windows and adding capped `limit`/pagination, while keeping any full historical batch behavior on the CLI side if needed.

### [requirements] Weight badge does not use required semantic token badge styling — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/flywheel/FlywheelStatusDetails.tsx:103`
FR-9 requires the weight badge to follow the existing semantic badge idiom from `statusPrimitives.tsx`, using semantic token classes such as `border-info/30`, `bg-info/15`, `text-info-foreground`, and `font-mono`. The current `WeightBadge` uses hardcoded amber classes, no border, and no `font-mono`.

This violates an explicit acceptance criterion for the UI surface. Fix by restyling the badge with the existing semantic-token badge pattern and extending the component test to assert those classes.

## Non-blocking Findings

### [requirements] Service tie-break diverges from vBRIEF action text
~ The b4-service action text says weighted rows should sort by weight descending, then `filed_at` ascending. The implementation sorts equal weights by `issueId`, and the tests document that behavior. The requirements reviewer treated this as advisory because it was not a separate acceptance criterion.

## Clean Sub-roles

pipeline.inspectNotes: Bead b3-weight-fn BLOCKED: commit d813b8b4 does not implement computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteria, stats) at all. The diff only adds optional weight/weightReason fields to the FlywheelSuggestion interface/schema in packages/contracts/src/flywheel.ts:180-190 — no status-multiplier logic, no normalizedDistance calculation, no compound-value field reading (medianMs/p95Ms), no insufficient_data short-circuit, and no reason-string generation exist anywhere in this commit. None of AC1-AC5 can be evaluated because the function under review is absent. This is the same d813b8b4 diff already submitted (and blocked) against bead b2-parse-criteria moments ago — it looks like the wrong commit is being routed to review requests, or the actual b3-weight-fn implementation commit has not landed yet. Required fix: identify and deliver the commit that actually adds computeSubstrateBugWeight, implementing per-criterion status multiplier (red=1.6x per AC1 example: 3*(1+0.6)), a status floor that dominates over raw normalized drift for red vs green (AC2), safe reading of a configured valueField from compound values with graceful fallback to normalizedDistance 0 + floor when the field is absent (AC3), a weight-0 + insufficient-telemetry-reason short circuit when all criteria are insufficient_data (AC4), and a reason string naming the highest-contributing criterion by label/status/value-vs-target (AC5).
